q.t: Which word is a noun? The happy child sang loudly.
q.e: ‘child’ names a person — you can say ‘the child’. ‘happy’ describes, ‘sang’ is an action, ‘loudly’ tells how.

q.t: Which is a proper noun?
q.e: Mumbai names one particular city, so it is proper and takes a capital letter.

q.t: Choose the collective noun: a ___ of sheep
q.e: Sheep (and birds) come in a flock. Cows come in a herd, bees in a swarm, wolves in a pack.

q.t: Which is an abstract noun?
q.e: Kindness is a quality — you can feel it but not touch it.

q.t: What is the plural of box?
q.e: Words ending in x take -es; ‘boxs’ can’t be said clearly, so -es adds the extra sound.

q.t: What is the plural of baby?
q.e: Consonant (b) + y → change y to i and add -es.

q.t: What is the plural of child?
q.e: ‘child’ has an old irregular plural: children (already plural — never ‘childrens’).

q.t: What is the feminine of king?
q.e: king → queen. (prince → princess.)

q.t: Choose the correct one: This is ___ bag. (it belongs to Riya)
q.e: One owner, Riya, so add ’s.

q.t: Which noun is uncountable?
q.e: You can’t count ‘one milk, two milks’; you count the container: a glass of milk.

q.t: What is the plural of leaf?
q.e: Most nouns ending in f change f to v and add -es: leaf → leaves, wolf → wolves.

q.t: What is the plural of roof?
q.e: roof is an exception to the f → ves rule: roofs (also chiefs, cliffs).

q.t: What is the plural of potato?
q.e: Many nouns ending in consonant + o add -es: potatoes, tomatoes, heroes.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She gave me some good advice.
She gave me some good advices.
She gave me a good advice.
She gave me many good advices.
q.e: ‘advice’ is uncountable — no plural and no ‘a’. Say ‘some advice’ or ‘a piece of advice’.

q.t: Choose the correct word: There isn't ___ sugar left.
q.e: Sugar is uncountable, so use ‘much’. ‘many’ and ‘a few’ go with countable plurals.

q.t: Which is a material noun?
q.e: Silver is a substance things are made of. A spoon is a thing (common noun) that may be made of silver.

q.t: Choose the correct possessive: The ___ hostel is near the gate. (many girls)
q.e: The owners are ‘girls’ (plural, already ending in s) — add just the apostrophe after the s.

q.t: Choose the correct possessive: This is the ___ section of the library.
q.e: ‘children’ is plural but does not end in s, so add ’s, just like a singular.

q.t: Form the abstract noun from brave.
q.e: brave → bravery. (‘bravely’ is an adverb, not a noun.)

q.t: Which noun is of COMMON gender?
q.e: A doctor can be a man or a woman. ‘table’ is neuter (neither); nephew is masculine; actress feminine.

q.t: Choose the correct verb: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
q.e: Mathematics looks plural (ends in s) but is the name of one subject, so it takes a singular verb.

q.t: Choose the correct verb: My new scissors ___ very sharp.
q.e: Scissors have two matching blades and are always plural. (‘A pair of scissors is …’ — then the verb follows ‘pair’.)

q.t: Which sentence is correct?
o: We bought new furniture for the room.
We bought new furnitures for the room.
We bought a new furniture for the room.
We bought many furnitures for the room.
q.e: Furniture is uncountable: no -s, no ‘a’. To count it, say ‘pieces of furniture’.

q.t: Identify the kind of the underlined noun: The jury has given its verdict.
q.e: A jury is a group of people acting as one unit — a collective noun.

q.t: Which is the correct plural?
q.e: In compound nouns the main word takes the plural. A son-in-law is a kind of son, so ‘sons’ changes.

q.t: What is the plural of mouse (the animal)?
q.e: mouse → mice, like louse → lice: an old vowel change.

q.t: Identify the abstract noun: His childhood was spent in the village.
q.e: Childhood is a stage of life — an idea, not something you can touch.

q.t: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
q.e: Belonging ‘its’ has no apostrophe. ‘it’s’ always means ‘it is’ or ‘it has’.

q.t: Choose the feminine form of host.
q.e: host → hostess (like actor → actress, waiter → waitress).

q.t: Which noun is ALWAYS uncountable?
q.e: You can have three messages or letters, but not ‘three informations’. Say ‘three pieces of information’.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
q.e: ‘news’ ends in s but is singular and uncountable: ‘The news is …’, ‘a piece of news’.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
q.e: The owner is ‘James’ (one person). Keep the full name and add ’s: James's. (James' is also seen, but never Jame's — that would make the name ‘Jame’.)

q.t: Which group contains ONLY uncountable nouns?
q.e: bag, idea and bottle can all be counted (two bags, many ideas). luggage, rice and honesty cannot.

q.t: Choose the correct one: I have two ___ to give you.
q.e: Advice is uncountable, so you count the ‘pieces’. ‘advise’ (with s) is the verb.

q.t: Identify the kind of noun: A Shakespeare is not born every day.
o: Proper noun used as a common noun
q.e: Here ‘a Shakespeare’ means ‘a great writer like Shakespeare’ — any one of a kind. A proper noun used like this behaves as a common noun (note the ‘a’).

q.t: Choose the correct plural: Both my ___ are doctors.
q.e: Pluralise the main noun (brother); ‘in-law’ just describes it.

q.t: Which is the correct plural of photo?
q.e: Short forms (photo from photograph, piano from pianoforte) just add -s.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: The cattle are grazing in the field.
The cattle is grazing in the field.
The cattles are grazing in the field.
A cattle is grazing in the field.
q.e: ‘cattle’ has no singular form and is always treated as plural: ‘The cattle are …’. One animal is ‘a cow’.

q.t: Form the abstract noun from the verb decide.
q.e: decide → decision (like divide → division). ‘decisive’ is an adjective.

q.t: In a two-hour journey, why is it hour and not hours?
o: ‘two-hour’ is used as an adjective, and adjectives have no plural
it should be ‘hours’ — this is wrong
q.e: Joined with a hyphen, ‘two-hour’ describes the journey. English adjectives never take -s, so: a ten-rupee note, a five-year-old girl.
